text:
Jamal: Need advice — booked an international return on the company card, had to cancel last-minute. Airline won't refund, they issued a travel credit/voucher in my name. I used the company card originally. Can I use the voucher for a personal trip later, or do I need to reimburse the company?
Ava (People Ops): Short: you cannot use a company-paid credit for personal travel without reimbursing. Options: reimburse the company for the credit value, or transfer the credit to the company if the airline allows and Finance approves.
Jamal: If I reimburse, how do I record it? Invoice the company? Negative expense?
Sam (Finance): Two accepted workflows: 1) Reimburse via the private-pay portal (we'll post a private-pay link). 2) Create an expense where you list the original charge as normal and then add a negative line item representing the voucher reimbursement (attach airline credit email + bank transfer proof). We prefer private-pay because it ties cleanly to the original corporate charge.
Ella (Travel Ops): Addendum: get the airline credit code and the full email PDF. Some airlines issue non-transferable credits; if it's non-transferable, company can't use it. In that case, reimbursement is required for personal use.
Jamal: What if I use the voucher to rebook a later flight that covers part business, part personal?
Ava (People Ops): Split usage rules apply. If the voucher covers a trip with both business and personal legs, you must allocate the business portion to the company. Provide the new itinerary, show which legs are business, and either: (a) have the airline reissue separate receipts for business vs personal legs (best), or (b) submit the single invoice plus a calc showing business portion and evidence of the business meeting/dates.
Sam (Finance): Also — if the airline applied the voucher against a future booking but left a residual balance, treat the residual like a credit. If you intend to keep any residual for personal use, reimburse that residual amount to the company.
Jamal: Suppose company-paid ticket had refundable add-ons (extra baggage) and those got refunded to company, but voucher equals ticket portion only. Any nuance?
Ella (Travel Ops): Keep itemized docs. Airlines often refund taxes/fees differently from fare. Upload the itemized refund/credit statement. Finance will reconcile tax/fee refunds separately.
Jamal: Example of how to enter this in the expense system?
Sam (Finance): Example (single expense submission with multiple line items):
```
Line 1: Flight (original corporate card charge)
  Amount: 1,200.00 USD
  Currency: USD
  Notes: Original itinerary 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-10, corporate card used, attach booking confirmation and card txn.
Line 2: Airline credit applied to personal rebooking (reimbursement to company)
  Amount: -900.00 USD
  Currency: USD
  Notes: Airline voucher code ABC123 issued 2026-07-20; used for 2026-11-05 booking. Attach voucher email + proof of reimbursement (bank tx or private-pay receipt).
Line 3: Personal seat upgrade on rebooking (employee-paid)
  Amount: 150.00 USD
  Currency: USD
  Notes: Paid from personal card; attach receipt and confirm not company business.
```
Sam (Finance): If you reimburse via private-pay, include the private-pay receipt in the expense and mark the negative line item as cleared. If you submit a bank transfer outside the portal, include the bank statement showing the exact transfer referencing the original invoice or voucher code.
Jamal: What about vouchers that expire? If the voucher expires and I didnt reimburse, does company absorb the loss?
Ava (People Ops): If the voucher arose from a company-paid business cancellation (e.g., company canceled event), Finance may treat it as company asset and decide how to use it. But if the cancellation was personal (employee-initiated change) and the voucher was issued in the employee's name, the employee is expected to reimburse the company if they use it personally. If a voucher expires with a value that should have been reimbursed, Finance will follow up to collect.
ExpenseBot: Reminder: do not use company-paid credits for personal travel without explicit Finance approval. See policy: People Ops > Travel > Refunds & credits. :warning:
Jamal: Any VAT/tax notes? Flights usually have taxes non-reclaimable, but fees/taxes refunded might show up differently.
Sam (Finance): Right. Airlines' tax and fee refunds are itemized; we need the airline statement. For non-flight items (hotels, ground transport) VAT reclaim depends on supplier docs. Always attach the original credit/refund communication.
Ella (Travel Ops): If the airline can reissue a receipt showing the credit application against the new itinerary, grab that. It makes reconciliation much faster.
Jamal: Thanks. Can you DM me the private-pay link when youre ready so I can clear this quickly?
Ava (People Ops): Will do — DM incoming. If anyone else encounters this, ping travel-ops or Finance before using vouchers.
